channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Can traditional Chinese exercises help people with musculoskeletal disorders? - BJSM blog - social media's leading SEM voice
item.description: An umbrella review of 92 meta-analyses (1,744 trials) found high-certainty evidence that Traditional Chinese Exercises (TCEs) improved physical function and mental health in knee osteoarthritis, mental health in neck pain, and sleep quality in fibromyalgia. Tai Chi reduced chronic MSD-related pain and stiffness and increased bone mineral density in osteopenia/osteoporosis.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Immediate task-specific and delayed generalized adaptations to variable dual-task training in community-dwelling older adults: a randomized waitlist-controlled trial
item.description: A 12-week variable dual-task training program for older adults (n=50) led to immediate gains in functional lower-limb strength (5xSTS: SMD = 0.54) and delayed improvements in functional mobility, inhibitory control, and short-term memory at 3-month follow-up.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Interval Between Injury and Surgery Influences Knee Biomechanics During Walking in Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstructed Patients: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 studies (18-55 years) found ACLR patients have lower peak knee flexion angle (SMD = -0.33), peak knee adduction angle (SMD = -0.47), and peak knee flexion moment (SMD = -0.64) during walking. Delayed reconstruction (≥ 12 months) is associated with persistent sagittal plane deficits, while early surgery (< 6 months) is linked to fewer long-term sagittal-plane deficits but temporary frontal-plane asymmetries and extension deficits.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exercise-based rehabilitation interventions for kinesiophobia after total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 RCTs (N = 1,096) found that exercise-based rehabilitation was associated with a reduction in kinesiophobia (SMD = -1.22) and improvements in knee function (SMD = 1.19) at ≤ 4 weeks post-TKA, although the certainty of evidence was low.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Effects of Neurostimulation- and Technology-Augmented Robot-Assisted Training on Upper-Limb Motor Recovery After Stroke: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of 103 trials (N = 5,251) found rTMS plus robot-assisted training (RAT) yielded the largest FMA-UE estimate (MD 9.56 points), followed by LFES plus RAT (MD 7.52) compared to usual care, with RAT alone showing smaller gains (MD 3.83).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of Incorporating Perceptual Learning Into Plantar Hardness Discrimination on the Risk of Falling and Muscle Torque in Patients With Hemiplegia: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=34) found that incorporating perceptual learning into plantar hardness discrimination significantly lowered fall risk (ES=1.48), increased knee extensor torque (ES=1.19), and improved FIM scores (ES=1.56) in hemiplegic stroke patients compared to a control group.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative effectiveness of different physical therapies for axillary web syndrome after breast cancer surgery: A network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
item.description: A network meta-analysis of 14 RCTs (1007 patients) found that soft tissue manual therapy + therapeutic exercise + low-level laser therapy significantly reduced pain (SMD = -4.40) and improved shoulder abduction (MD = 59.51) and flexion (MD = 77.30) in axillary web syndrome. Manual lymphatic drainage + therapeutic exercise showed the largest improvement in upper-limb disability (MD = -19.01).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of Manual Physiotherapy Techniques for Improving Cervical Range of Motion in Infants With Congenital Muscular Torticollis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of five RCTs (n=143 infants) found a statistically significant pooled effect (Cohen's d = 0.90, 95% CI: 0.54 to 1.27, p < 0.001) in favor of manual physiotherapy techniques for improving cervical ROM in infants with congenital muscular torticollis.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Altered Cognitive Control and Cortical Oscillatory Dynamics in Athletes With ACL Reconstruction During Decision-Making Under Uncertainty.
item.description: A study of 90 open-skill athletes (45 non-ACLR, 45 ACLR) found ACLR athletes exhibited slower response times and lower accuracy (d = 0.75-1.09) during a probabilistic go/no-go task, along with attenuated prestimulus midfrontal theta power (d = 0.60) and reduced left-lateralized central beta (d = 0.61) and posterior alpha suppression (d = 0.55) during target phase.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Diagnosis, Rehabilitation, and Return to Sport after Athletic Hamstring Injury: An ICCUS Society Consensus Statement.
item.description: An ICCUS Society consensus statement, developed via a modified Delphi process with 17 experts, achieved 89.88% agreement on 54 out of 60 statements regarding athletic hamstring injury management. Key recommendations include standardized terminology, criterion-based rehabilitation, progressive tissue loading, and integrating various factors for return to sport decisions.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of Exercise Type and Duration on Pain, Function, and Quality of Life in Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review With Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A Bayesian network meta-analysis of 35 trials (n = 3808 patients) found that short-term combined aerobic and resistance exercise had the largest effects on pain (SMD = -0.937, low certainty), function (SMD = -0.590, low certainty), and quality of life (SMD = 0.663, low certainty) in patients with knee osteoarthritis.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Efficacy of Low-Level Laser Therapy in Patients With Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 RCTs found low-level laser therapy (LLLT) significantly reduced pain (Hedges' g=-1.524, P <0.001) and improved grip strength (Hedges' g=0.391, P=0.002) in carpal tunnel syndrome. Pulsed mode was superior for analgesia, continuous for grip strength.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of chair-based exercise training on pulmonary function, exercise capacity, and quality of life in patients with acute exacerbation of COPD: A randomised controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=30) found that chair-based exercise training in patients hospitalized with acute COPD exacerbations significantly improved functional exercise capacity (mean 6MWT distance change 50.9 m [95% CI 2.09-99.76]; p=0.042), dyspnea, and quality of life compared to breathing exercises alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Five Days of Acute Intermittent Hypoxia Is Safe and Improves Somatic Motor Function in Persons with Multiple Sclerosis
item.description: A randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled crossover trial (n=23 MS patients) found that 5 days of acute intermittent hypoxia (AIH) significantly increased ankle plantarflexion torque (beta = 8.74 Nm, p < 0.001) and 6-minute walk distance (beta = 10.14 m, p = 0.039) compared to Sham, with no serious adverse events.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Neurocognitive Factors in ACL Injury: The Missing Piece in Rehabilitation and Prevention? A Scoping Review.
item.description: A scoping review of 42 studies published between 2006 and 2026 suggests neurocognitive factors, particularly dual-task interference and visual attention, are significant contributors to ACL injury and should be integrated into rehabilitation and return-to-sport testing. Neurocognitive training interventions show potential benefits in improving visuomotor efficiency and movement compliance.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of sleep manipulation on athletic performance, cognitive function, and recovery: a systematic review of experimental studies
item.description: A systematic review of 15 experimental studies found that sleep extension generally led to enhanced athletic performance (e.g., +9.5 m in shuttle run, -0.7 s in sprint time, ~3% improvement in endurance), cognitive function, and recovery. Sleep restriction had adverse effects, while daytime napping showed mixed, context-dependent results.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Effectiveness of wearable and non-wearable biofeedback on knee biomechanics during functional tasks in anterior cruciate ligament injury prevention and rehabilitation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found that biofeedback interventions significantly reduced peak knee abduction angle (Hedges’ g = 0.52, 95% CI 0.06 to 0.98) in ACL injury prevention, but the certainty of evidence was low to very low, with no significant effects on other knee biomechanics.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Physiological responses during high intensity interval training and moderate intensity continuous training in patients attending early cardiac rehabilitation.
item.description: In 18 cardiac rehabilitation patients, low-volume HIIT elicited greater ventilatory, hemodynamic, and metabolic demands (e.g., higher mean VO₂, %HRR, blood lactate) and higher perceived exertion compared to time-matched MICT, suggesting a greater physiological stimulus.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The development and psychometric evaluation of the Post Activity Symptom Scale (PASS) for Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/ Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.
item.description: A new scale, the Post Activity Symptom Scale (PASS), was developed and psychometrically evaluated for measuring post-exertional malaise in people with ME/CFS, showing excellent test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.81) and moderate criterion-related validity (r=0.58).
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Feasibility of an interprofessional rehabilitation program (IPRehab-LBP) for people with chronic low back pain in Ethiopia: an open-label pilot randomized controlled trial with an embedded process evaluation
item.description: A pilot RCT in Ethiopia found an interprofessional rehabilitation program (IPRehab-LBP) for chronic low back pain to be feasible and acceptable, reducing disability (RMDQ mean difference, -6.29; 95% CI, -9.69 to -2.89) compared to usual care.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord
